subtopics.title: Why an Asset Disposal Account Exists

questions.question: The asset disposal account gathers:
options: The asset's COST, its accumulated depreciation, and the proceeds — weighed against each other in one place
The asset's market value and insurance value

questions.question: Posting the proceeds directly against the asset's cost is wrong because:
options: It is slower than using a disposal account
Selling price and cost are different amounts — the difference is a profit or loss belonging on the income statement, and both figures get corrupted
Proceeds belong in the capital account

questions.question: If the credits in the disposal account exceed the debits, the result is:
options: A PROFIT on disposal — the asset sold for more than its carrying value

questions.question: A profit or loss on disposal really represents:
options: A cash gain to the owner
An error in the original purchase price
A CORRECTION — the accumulated verdict on every depreciation estimate made across the asset's life

subtopics.title: The Four Steps That Never Vary

questions.question: Step one of every disposal is:
options: Bring DEPRECIATION UP TO DATE to the date of sale — the most commonly forgotten step and the one carrying the most marks

questions.question: A vehicle cost R240 000, depreciated 20% on diminishing balance, sold nine months into year three. The part-year depreciation is:
options: R23 040 — 20% of the R153 600 carrying value, for nine of twelve months

questions.question: Transferring the cost to the disposal account is recorded as:
options: Debit the asset account, credit Asset Disposal
DEBIT Asset Disposal, CREDIT the asset account with the full original cost
Debit Accumulated Depreciation, credit the asset account

questions.question: With cost R240 000, accumulated depreciation R109 440 and proceeds R122 000, the result is:
options: A LOSS of R8 560 — proceeds R122 000 against a carrying value of R130 560

subtopics.title: Timing, and the Four Kinds of Disposal

questions.question: An asset sold on the FIRST day of the financial year:
options: Needs NO additional depreciation — the accumulated figure is simply the balance brought forward

questions.question: An asset sold on credit creates:
options: A trade debtor recorded in Debtors Control
A SUNDRY or other debtor — the business does not trade in vehicles, so it belongs under other receivables

questions.question: Old bakkie traded in at R122 000 against a new one priced at R330 000, with R208 000 paid in cash. The new asset is recorded at:
options: R330 000 — the full cost; the trade-in was real value forming part of the payment

questions.question: An owner taking a vehicle worth R122 000 but recording drawings of R30 000 has:
options: Understated their withdrawals and overstated the business's equity — a misstatement an auditor traces against carrying value and market evidence

subtopics.title: The Register, the Controls and the Ethics

questions.question: After a disposal, the asset register's totals:
options: Must still agree with the ledger's asset and accumulated depreciation balances — a mismatch signals a control failure
Are updated only at year end

questions.question: Requiring quotes or a valuation before disposal exists to:
options: Show the price was REASONABLE rather than a favour to a friend or relative — the point where nepotism enters

questions.question: Segregation of duties at disposal means:
options: Assets are sold only for cash
The person who AUTHORISES the disposal should not be the person who receives the money or updates the records
One person handles the whole transaction for accountability

questions.question: The classic disposal fraud is:
options: Recording a trade-in at full cost
Selling an asset at a profit
Selling the asset, pocketing the proceeds, and writing it off as scrapped — defeated by independent authorisation plus a register reconciled to the ledger

subtopics.title: What the Books Still Think It's Worth

questions.question: The books' answer to "what is the bakkie worth?" is:
options: The carrying value — cost minus everything written off for wear, R130 560

questions.question: The temporary "desk" opened for the transaction:
options: Is the ASSET DISPOSAL account — opened for one deal, weighed, and cleared away the same day

questions.question: The R8 560 loss means:
options: The business traded badly this year
The books' depreciation guess was slightly off — reality checked the estimate on the day of sale

subtopics.title: Four Moves, Always the Same Order

questions.question: The move everybody forgets is:
options: CATCH UP THE WEAR — the months driven in the final year, written off before anything else
Putting the cost on the desk

questions.question: The amount of wear placed on the desk is:
options: R109 440 — everything ever written off, including the caught-up R23 040

questions.question: The five-second check that catches nearly every mistake is:
options: Comparing what the books said it was worth against what was actually received — the gap must equal your answer

questions.question: If the long method and the quick check disagree, the usual culprit is:
options: An error in the accumulated total brought forward
The forgotten part-year wear from move one

subtopics.title: Cash, Credit, Trade-In, or Uncle Takes It Home

questions.question: The buyer of the bakkie from a building-materials business is:
options: A once-off debtor, filed separately from customers who buy stock
A trade debtor in Debtors Control

questions.question: Recording the new bakkie at the R208 000 cash handed over:
options: Is correct, since that is what left the bank
UNDERSTATES the asset by R122 000 — and makes every depreciation charge for the next five years wrong too

questions.question: When the owner keeps the bakkie for the family, the entry is:
options: A cash sale at market value
DRAWINGS at an honest value — the owner helping himself to business property

questions.question: An asset scrapped or given away produces:
options: A profit equal to the accumulated depreciation
A loss equal to the WHOLE remaining book value, since nothing was received
